001_init.sql:
-- Scheduler skeleton · initial schema
-- Corresponds to docs/scheduler-spec.md §9; fields/tables marked [supplemental] are required by the implementation but not listed in the spec.

BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Clock
-- All timestamps come from app_now(), not the process clock and not the now() literal.
-- In production offset_ms is always 0, so app_now() is equivalent to now();
-- Tests use it to "time travel" instead of actually sleeping 45 seconds waiting for SUSPECT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _clock (
  id        BOOLEAN PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (id),
  offset_ms BIGINT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
INSERT INTO _clock (id, offset_ms) VALUES (TRUE, 0) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION app_now() RETURNS timestamptz
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
  SELECT now() + make_interval(secs => (SELECT offset_ms / 1000.0 FROM _clock LIMIT 1))
$$;

-- Effective priority after aging: lower numbers are higher priority (P0 is highest).
-- P0 does not age; everything else gains one level per full aging_after_seconds, capped at P1.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION effective_priority(
  p_priority SMALLINT, p_enqueued TIMESTAMPTZ, p_aging INTEGER DEFAULT 600
) RETURNS INTEGER
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
  SELECT CASE
    WHEN p_priority = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE GREATEST(1, p_priority - (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (app_now() - p_enqueued)) / p_aging)::int)
  END
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Config tables (owned by PCS, read-only to the scheduler)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_definitions (
  task_type        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_version     TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_role      TEXT NOT NULL,
  capabilities     TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  input_schema     JSONB,
  output_schema    JSONB,
  default_profile  TEXT,
  max_attempts     SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
  retryable_errors TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'   -- [supplemental] Empty means "everything is retryable except non-retryable errors"
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resource_profiles (
  profile_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  cpu_millicores  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  memory_bytes    BIGINT NOT NULL,
  disk_bytes      BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  timeout_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3600
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hosts (
  host_id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name                TEXT NOT NULL,
  os                  TEXT NOT NULL,
  arch                TEXT NOT NULL,
  host_state          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (host_state IN
                        ('NORMAL','WARNING','THROTTLED','PROTECTING','RECOVERING')),
  cpu_total           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 4,
  mem_total_bytes     BIGINT NOT NULL,
  mem_available_bytes BIGINT NOT NULL,
  updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_instances (
  instance_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  role_id            TEXT NOT NULL,
  host_id            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES hosts(host_id),
  state              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN
                       ('PROVISIONING','STARTING','ONLINE','SUSPECT','DRAINING','OFFLINE','FAILED')),
  agent_profile_id   TEXT,
  allowed_task_types TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  capabilities       JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{"healthy":[]}',
  config_version     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  protocol_version   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0',
  payload_schemas    TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY['1.0'],
  last_heartbeat_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  load               JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  -- [supplemental] drain deadline: not finished in time → OFFLINE (§7.10)
  drain_deadline_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  -- [supplemental] Capability ceiling configured in PCS: the capabilities endpoint can only narrow, not widen (§7.3)
  capability_ceiling TEXT[],
  registered_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduler_config (
  id                  BOOLEAN PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (id),
  global_limit        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
  role_pool_limit     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 20,
  instance_limit      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  task_type_limit     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,
  aging_after_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 600,
  lease_seconds       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 300,
  start_window_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,
  suspect_after_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 45,
  offline_after_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 90,
  retry_backoff_seconds INTEGER[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY[300, 900, 2700],  -- 5m → 15m → 45m
  updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
INSERT INTO scheduler_config (id) VALUES (TRUE) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- Idempotent column additions: this skeleton has no migration tool, so re-running 001 patches an old database
ALTER TABLE scheduler_config
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS retry_backoff_seconds INTEGER[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY[300, 900, 2700];
ALTER TABLE role_instances
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS drain_deadline_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_ceiling TEXT[];

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Workflows
-- Templates are maintained by PCS; the scheduler is read-only (§7.1)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_templates (
  workflow_template_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name                 TEXT NOT NULL,
  version              TEXT NOT NULL,
  phases               JSONB NOT NULL,
  approval_policy_ref  TEXT,
  created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_runs (
  workflow_run_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  workflow_template_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  template_version     TEXT NOT NULL,
  status               TEXT NOT NULL,
  current_phase        TEXT,
  root_task_id         TEXT,
  -- [supplemental] Task for the current phase; the APPROVE phase has no task, so the previous phase task is kept for binding the approval subject
  current_task_id      TEXT,
  -- [supplemental] Cross-phase context (priority, resource profile, etc.), copied to the next phase task on advance
  context              JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  updated_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

ALTER TABLE workflow_runs
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS current_task_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS context JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';

-- Pending approvals (§7.3): approvals is written only after the decision; this records "who must approve what".
-- Created after tasks because task_id has a foreign key.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Tasks
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
  task_id               TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_type             TEXT NOT NULL,
  task_version          TEXT NOT NULL,
  workflow_run_id       TEXT REFERENCES workflow_runs(workflow_run_id),
  parent_task_id        TEXT REFERENCES tasks(task_id),
  priority_class        SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (priority_class BETWEEN 0 AND 3),
  status                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN
                          ('QUEUED','ASSIGNED','RUNNING','SUCCEEDED','FAILED','BLOCKED','CANCELLED')),
  payload_ref           TEXT,
  payload_sha256        TEXT,
  payload_schema        TEXT NOT NULL,
  requirements          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  resource_profile_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES resource_profiles(profile_id),
  resource_block_reason TEXT,
  resource_evaluated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  attempt_count         SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  max_attempts          SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
  current_attempt_id    TEXT,
  enqueued_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  deadline_at           TIMESTAMPTZ,
  cancel_requested_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  -- [supplemental] Backoff window: non-null and not yet elapsed means not claimable
  next_attempt_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  -- [supplemental] Dead-letter marker
  dead_letter           BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  version               BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  updated_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approval_requests (
  approval_request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  workflow_run_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES workflow_runs(workflow_run_id),
  task_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(task_id),
  status              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN
                         ('PENDING','APPROVED','REJECTED','INVALIDATED','EXPIRED')),
  subject_digest      TEXT,
  action_scope        TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  policy_version      TEXT,
  requested_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  decided_at          TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS approval_requests_one_pending
  ON approval_requests (task_id) WHERE status = 'PENDING';

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_attempts (
  attempt_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id           TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(task_id),
  attempt_number    SMALLINT NOT NULL,
  instance_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  host_id           TEXT NOT NULL,
  agent_profile_id  TEXT,
  status            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN
                      ('CREATED','STARTED','SUCCEEDED','FAILED','CANCELLED','TIMEOUT')),
  result_summary    TEXT,
  outputs           JSONB,
  error             JSONB,
  started_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
  finished_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  UNIQUE (task_id, attempt_number)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leases (
  lease_token       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id           TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(task_id),
  attempt_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES task_attempts(attempt_id),
  instance_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  fencing_token     BIGINT NOT NULL,
  issued_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  expires_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  released_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  release_reason    TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_events (
  event_id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id           TEXT NOT NULL,
  event_type        TEXT NOT NULL,
  from_status       TEXT,
  to_status         TEXT,
  actor             TEXT,
  payload           JSONB,
  trace_id          TEXT,
  created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

-- Reliable event source (protocol §8.1): written in the same transaction as state transitions, append-only.
-- SSE / polling notifications both read from here; notifications may be lost, but only this table is source of truth.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outbox_events (
  event_id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  event_type        TEXT NOT NULL,
  schema_version    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0',
  aggregate_type    TEXT NOT NULL,
  aggregate_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  aggregate_version BIGINT,
  occurred_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  trace_id          TEXT,
  actor_id          TEXT,
  idempotency_key   TEXT,
  payload           JSONB
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approvals (
  approval_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id           TEXT NOT NULL,
  workflow_run_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  decision          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('APPROVED','REJECTED')),
  operator_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  comment           TEXT,
  approval_token    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  subject_digest    TEXT NOT NULL,
  action_scope      TEXT[] NOT NULL,
  policy_version    TEXT NOT NULL,
  invalidated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  decided_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

-- jti of the approval token: a token can be persisted only once
ALTER TABLE approvals ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS token_jti TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS approvals_token_jti
  ON approvals (token_jti) WHERE token_jti IS NOT NULL;
-- Approvals with no bound digest (e.g. workflows without artifacts) may be null
ALTER TABLE approvals ALTER COLUMN subject_digest DROP NOT NULL;

-- Artifacts (§7.8): the scheduler records only metadata and storage references, never parses content.
-- declared_sha256 is declared by the uploader; on complete the server recomputes actual_sha256 and compares.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS artifacts (
  artifact_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(task_id),
  attempt_id      TEXT REFERENCES task_attempts(attempt_id),
  instance_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('PENDING','COMPLETE','FAILED')),
  declared_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
  actual_sha256   TEXT,
  size_bytes      BIGINT,
  media_type      TEXT,
  storage_ref     TEXT,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS artifacts_task_idx ON artifacts (task_id, status);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resource_reservations (
  grant_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  host_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
  instance_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  task_id         TEXT,
  attempt_id      TEXT,
  profile_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('DEPLOYMENT','TASK')),
  state           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('HELD','ACTIVE','RELEASED','RECLAIMED')),
  cpu_millicores  INTEGER,
  memory_bytes    BIGINT,
  disk_bytes      BIGINT,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  activated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  closed_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  close_reason    TEXT,
  CHECK (kind <> 'TASK' OR (task_id IS NOT NULL AND attempt_id IS NOT NULL))
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Invariants
-- Events are append-only: any UPDATE/DELETE raises an error (§4.4)
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION append_only() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'task_events is append-only (attempted %)', TG_OP;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS task_events_append_only ON task_events;
CREATE TRIGGER task_events_append_only
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON task_events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION append_only();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS outbox_events_append_only ON outbox_events;
CREATE TRIGGER outbox_events_append_only
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON outbox_events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION append_only();

-- At most one unreleased lease per task at any moment (the last gate against duplicate claims by multiple instances)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leases_one_active_per_task
  ON leases (task_id) WHERE released_at IS NULL;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Indexes
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_claim_idx
  ON tasks (status, priority_class, enqueued_at, task_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_workflow_idx ON tasks (workflow_run_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_block_reason_idx
  ON tasks (resource_block_reason) WHERE resource_block_reason IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leases_expiry_idx
  ON leases (expires_at) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS task_events_task_idx ON task_events (task_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS outbox_events_aggregate_idx
  ON outbox_events (aggregate_type, aggregate_id, event_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS reservations_host_idx ON resource_reservations (host_id, state);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS instances_heartbeat_idx ON role_instances (last_heartbeat_at);

COMMIT;

003_profiles.sql:
-- P4: Agent / API Profile references in the task envelope.
-- The scheduler only stores/returns references; it does not parse Profile contents or touch secrets.

ALTER TABLE role_instances
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS agent_profile_version TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS api_profile_ids TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';
004_chat_console.sql:
-- 004: Chat and builder terminal
--
-- Neither chat nor terminal is a "bypass": like builds, they are ordinary tasks on the scheduler,
-- subject to allowed_task_types, resource profiles, leases, fencing, timeouts and auditing.
--
-- v4 constraints:
--   * task.chat.builder / task.chat.scheduler can be routed to an Agent
--     (Claude Code / Codex, etc.), and the Agent sees only this message and explicit history.
--   * task.console.builder runs a full shell inside the builder container, equivalent to SSH;
--     there is no command allowlist. Isolation relies on container boundaries, resource limits and network policy.
--   * console tasks have max attempts fixed at 1: never retry blindly when the command result is uncertain.

INSERT INTO task_definitions (task_type, task_version, target_role, capabilities, default_profile, max_attempts) VALUES
  ('task.chat.builder',      '1.0', 'builder',   ARRAY['llm','shell'], 'rp_builder_small', 1),
  ('task.chat.scheduler',    '1.0', 'scheduler', ARRAY['llm'],         'rp_control',       1),
  ('task.console.builder',   '1.0', 'builder',   ARRAY['shell'],       'rp_builder_small', 1),
  ('task.console.scheduler', '1.0', 'scheduler', ARRAY['shell'],       'rp_control',       1)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- Add the corresponding task types to already-registered instances; appended only once, so re-running the migration is idempotent.
UPDATE role_instances
   SET allowed_task_types = allowed_task_types || ARRAY['task.chat.' || role_id]
 WHERE role_id IN ('builder', 'scheduler')
   AND NOT ('task.chat.' || role_id = ANY(allowed_task_types));

UPDATE role_instances
   SET allowed_task_types = allowed_task_types || ARRAY['task.console.' || role_id]
 WHERE role_id IN ('builder', 'scheduler')
   AND NOT ('task.console.' || role_id = ANY(allowed_task_types));

-- and task_definitions decides whether a task_type is known). Each host has its own scheduler database,
-- and should accept tasks without the seed, so these two blocks live here and always run with migrations.

INSERT INTO resource_profiles (profile_id, cpu_millicores, memory_bytes, disk_bytes, timeout_seconds) VALUES

  ('rp_builder_medium', 2000, 4294967296, 34359738368, 3600),

INSERT INTO task_definitions (task_type, task_version, target_role, capabilities, default_profile, max_attempts) VALUES

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
006_capability.sql:
-- 006: Capability score (W) and task difficulty (D), plus node scheduler reporting.
--
-- W is computed by whoever creates the builder as an integer 0–1000, weighting six items: cores/frequency/memory/disk/model/API,
-- and written to role_instances with the registration request; the scheduler filters claims by D <= W.
-- D = 0 means "unrestricted", compatible with pre-upgrade historical tasks and instances that never reported W.

ALTER TABLE role_instances
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE role_instances
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_detail jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;

ALTER TABLE tasks
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS difficulty integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_claim_difficulty_idx
  ON tasks (difficulty) WHERE status = 'QUEUED';

-- Aggregated capability reported by child schedulers. Each level stores only direct children; the tree is reconstructed from parent_node_id;
-- subtree_score is computed recursively by the child itself and simply summed by the parent, avoiding repeated whole-tree traversal.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduler_nodes (
  node_id text PRIMARY KEY,
  parent_node_id text NULL,
  host_id text NOT NULL,
  role text NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('root', 'node')),
  local_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  subtree_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  builder_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  child_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS scheduler_nodes_parent_idx
  ON scheduler_nodes (parent_node_id);
008_dynamic_scheduling.sql:
-- 008: Dynamic scheduling (v0.3)
--
-- Adds the scheduler-side ledger for static/dynamic scheduling:
--   * host resource pool capacity and live cgroup metrics
--   * per-instance cap / demand / live capability fields
--   * grant generations applied by host-runtime (PENDING -> APPLIED)
--   * durable claim backoff fields, so a blocked head-of-line task no longer stalls the queue
--
-- The file is idempotent: every migration re-runs on an existing database.

BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Queue / admission tuning
ALTER TABLE scheduler_config
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_candidate_scan integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 20,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backoff_base_seconds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backoff_max_seconds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 60,
  -- How many tasks of one type a single builder may run at once (§9.1 k_max).
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS task_type_instance_limit integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 4,
  -- Consecutive task-specific resource blocks before the task is marked unschedulable.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_blocked_attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 8,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scheduling_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'static',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS dynamic_policy jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'scheduler_config_scheduling_mode_chk'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE scheduler_config
      ADD CONSTRAINT scheduler_config_scheduling_mode_chk
      CHECK (scheduling_mode IN ('static', 'dynamic'));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Instance capability / capacity
ALTER TABLE role_instances
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scheduling_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'static',
  -- Instance cap: deployment resource_profile, in the scheduler's integer units.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cap_cpu_millicores integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cap_mem_bytes bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- v0.3 capability split. capability_score remains the legacy frozen W for compatibility.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_static_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_ceiling_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_live_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_dispatch_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_guaranteed_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_schema_version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS capability_updated_at timestamptz,
  -- Latest per-instance usage reported by host-runtime; used for demand only.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS usage_mem_bytes bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS usage_cpu_millicores integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS usage_updated_at timestamptz;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'role_instances_scheduling_mode_chk'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE role_instances
      ADD CONSTRAINT role_instances_scheduling_mode_chk
      CHECK (scheduling_mode IN ('static', 'dynamic'));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Task head-of-line blocking
ALTER TABLE tasks
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS resource_retry_after timestamptz,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS blocked_attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS unschedulable boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_claim_ready_idx
  ON tasks (status, resource_retry_after, enqueued_at)
  WHERE status = 'QUEUED' AND unschedulable = FALSE;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Host resource pool
-- One row per host. Capacity (C_mem/C_cpu) is the same number used by pool.slice
-- and by the fair-share ledger, so the account and the kernel limit never disagree.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS host_resource_pools (
  host_id                    text PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES hosts(host_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  pool_id                    text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'osacp.slice/pool.slice',
  cgroup_available           boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  cgroup_driver              text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cgroupfs',
  cpu_total_millicores       integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  mem_total_bytes            bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cpu_granted_millicores     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  mem_granted_bytes          bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cpu_used_millicores        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  mem_used_bytes             bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  mem_working_set_bytes      bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  available_commitment_bytes bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  pressure_state             text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NORMAL'
                               CHECK (pressure_state IN ('NORMAL','BUSY','PRESSURE','CRITICAL','RECOVERING')),
  psi                        jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  cgroup                     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  reported_at                timestamptz,
  updated_at                 timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Grants
-- One current grant row per instance. generation is monotonic per instance.
-- Host-runtime applies the values to the builder cgroup and reports them back as APPLIED.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resource_grants (
  host_id            text NOT NULL,
  instance_id        text NOT NULL,
  generation         bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  cpu_millicores     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  memory_bytes       bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  memory_low_bytes   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  memory_high_bytes  bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cpu_weight         integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  state              text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING'
                       CHECK (state IN ('PENDING','APPLYING','APPLIED','FAILED','SUPERSEDED')),
  applied_generation bigint,
  applied_cpu_millicores integer,
  applied_memory_bytes bigint,
  applied_memory_low_bytes bigint,
  applied_memory_high_bytes bigint,
  applied_cpu_weight integer,
  applied_at         timestamptz,
  last_error         text,
  updated_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (host_id, instance_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS resource_grants_state_idx
  ON resource_grants (host_id, state);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Federation snapshot
ALTER TABLE scheduler_nodes
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'static',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_builder_ceiling integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_builder_live integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS guaranteed_score integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS available_commitment_mem_bytes bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pressure_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NORMAL',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS stale boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;

-- Legacy rows: keep max_builder_score as the ceiling until the next report fills the new columns.
UPDATE scheduler_nodes
   SET max_builder_ceiling = GREATEST(max_builder_ceiling, max_builder_score)
 WHERE max_builder_ceiling = 0;

COMMIT;
009_agent_control.sql:
-- 009: Agent control (v0.4)
--
-- Three capabilities that all need durable scheduler state:
--   * NEEDS_INPUT: an attempt may stop and ask a person instead of failing or guessing.
--   * WAITING_CHILDREN: one task may be split into several child tasks that different
--     builders run in parallel; the parent resumes once every child is terminal.
--   * approval_mode + typed outcome: how much the executor may do without asking, and
--     what actually happened (done, denied, interrupted after an outward action, ...).
--
-- The file is idempotent: every migration re-runs on an existing database.

BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Defaults
ALTER TABLE scheduler_config
  -- Existing deployments run fully autonomous builders, so keep that as the default and let
  -- per-task or per-definition overrides tighten it. "ask" is never the default here: a
  -- stricter level than the deployment can execute would turn every build into a denial.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS default_approval_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'full',
  -- How long a task may wait for a person's answer before it expires.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS needs_input_ttl_seconds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 86400,
  -- Fan-out bounds: they keep a misbehaving agent from turning one task into an unbounded tree.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_fanout_children integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 16,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_fanout_depth integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 4,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_resume_rounds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 8;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'scheduler_config_approval_mode_chk'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE scheduler_config
      ADD CONSTRAINT scheduler_config_approval_mode_chk
      CHECK (default_approval_mode IN ('ask', 'edits', 'auto', 'full'));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Task control fields
ALTER TABLE tasks
  -- ask: ask before acting | edits: edit files freely, ask before commands |
  -- auto: act within the workspace | full: no further gate (the deployment's current behaviour)
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS approval_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'full',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS outcome text,
  -- The question an agent parked on; cleared when an answer resumes the task.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_question jsonb,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS needs_input_at timestamptz,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS needs_input_expires_at timestamptz,
  -- Set on a child task to the id of the task that split it. parent_task_id is also set, but
  -- it is shared with workflow phase chaining, so fan-out counting must not use it.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fanout_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fanout_depth smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fanout_rounds smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- Every resume (answer or settled children) counts here, not against the failure budget.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS resume_rounds smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

ALTER TABLE tasks DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS tasks_status_check;
ALTER TABLE tasks ADD CONSTRAINT tasks_status_check CHECK (status IN
  ('QUEUED','ASSIGNED','RUNNING','SUCCEEDED','FAILED','BLOCKED','CANCELLED',
   'NEEDS_INPUT','WAITING_CHILDREN'));

ALTER TABLE tasks DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS tasks_approval_mode_chk;
ALTER TABLE tasks ADD CONSTRAINT tasks_approval_mode_chk
  CHECK (approval_mode IN ('ask', 'edits', 'auto', 'full'));

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt control fields
ALTER TABLE task_attempts
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS outcome text,
  -- PARKED is an attempt that ended without success or failure and will be resumed by a new attempt.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS park_reason text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS parked_at timestamptz,
  -- Append-only list of outward actions observed before/while the attempt ran. Its presence
  -- is what stops a lease expiry from blindly re-running side effects on another machine.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS outward_actions jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb;

ALTER TABLE task_attempts DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS task_attempts_status_check;
ALTER TABLE task_attempts ADD CONSTRAINT task_attempts_status_check CHECK (status IN
  ('CREATED','STARTED','SUCCEEDED','FAILED','CANCELLED','TIMEOUT','PARKED'));

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_fanout_idx ON tasks (fanout_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tasks_needs_input_idx
  ON tasks (needs_input_expires_at) WHERE status = 'NEEDS_INPUT';

COMMIT;
010_failure_recovery.sql:
-- 010: Failure classification and recovery (v0.4)
--
-- A single retry policy is wrong for every failure:
--   * a usage/rate limit that resets in an hour is not solved by three short backoffs;
--   * a busy host is not a failure at all and must not consume the retry budget;
--   * a deterministic refusal is not retried at all.
-- The scheduler now classifies the failure first and then chooses the action. Waiting for an
-- external reset is bounded by retry_waivers so a permanently limited provider cannot park a task
-- forever. failure_class on the attempt records why, for the dead-letter view.
--
-- Idempotent: every migration re-runs on an existing database.

BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE tasks
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS retry_waivers smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

ALTER TABLE task_attempts
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS failure_class text,
  -- Grouping key over the normalized error text, so the same fleet-wide failure is one row.
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS failure_signature text;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS failure_signatures (
  signature     text PRIMARY KEY,
  kind          text NOT NULL,
  code          text NOT NULL,
  -- Normalized sample: paths, URLs, ids and numbers replaced; kept local as the readable title.
  sample        text,
  occurrences   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  first_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now(),
  last_seen_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT app_now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS failure_signatures_recent_idx
  ON failure_signatures (last_seen_at DESC);

COMMIT;
011_artifact_names.sql:
-- Artifact file names.
--
-- The artifact channel stores bytes and digests; the original name is needed to present a file
-- (download filename, task file list) instead of an opaque artifact id. The name is metadata only:
-- storage is still keyed by artifact_id and the digest is still recomputed by the server.
ALTER TABLE artifacts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS name TEXT;
